163: ### SystemVerilog Assertion Macros
164: 
165: The header file [`assertions.svh`](include/common_cells/assertions.svh) contains macros that expand to assertion blocks.
166: These macros should recduce the effort in writing many assertions and make it
167: easier to use them. They are similar to but incompatible with the macros used by [lowrisc](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_assert.sv).

169: #### Simple Assertion and Cover Macros
170: | Macro              | Arguments                                        | Description                                                                |
171: | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
172: | <code>`ASSERT_I</code>     | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__desc`)                   | Immediate assertion                                                        |
173: | <code>`ASSERT_INIT</code>  | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__desc`)                   | Assertion in initial block. Can be used for things like parameter checking |
174: | <code>`ASSERT_FINAL</code> | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__desc`)                   | Assertion in final block                                                   |
175: | <code>`ASSERT</code>       | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`) | Assert a concurrent property directly                                      |
176: | <code>`ASSERT_NEVER</code> | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`) | Assert a concurrent property NEVER happens                                 |
177: | <code>`ASSERT_KNOWN</code> | `__name`, `__sig`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`)  | Concurrent clocked assertion with custom error message                     |
178: | <code>`COVER</code>        | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`)           | Cover a concurrent property                                                |
179: - *The name of the clock and reset signals for implicit variants is `clk_i` and `rst_ni`, respectively.*
180: - *`__desc` is an optional string argument describing the failure causing the assertion to be violated that is embedded into the error report and defaults to `""`.*
